message.content:
**Earliest non‑Christian historical reference to Jesus Christ**

| Source | Date (approx.) | Passage | Significance |
|--------|----------------|---------|--------------|
| **Flavius Josephus – *Antiquities of the Jews*, Book 18, Chapter 3** | 93–94 CE | “Now there was about this time Jesus, a wise man, if it be lawful to call him a man… He was crucified by Pontius Pilate.” | This is the earliest surviving mention of Jesus in a contemporary Roman‑Jewish historian’s work. It appears in a passage that is widely accepted as authentic (though it contains a later Christian interpolation). |
| **Tacitus – *Annals*, Book 15, Chapter 44** | 116 CE | “Christus, the founder of the name, was executed by Pontius Pilate during the reign of Tiberius.” | A Roman imperial historian who was not a Christian, confirming the crucifixion and the existence of a movement called Christianity. |
| **Pliny the Younger – *Letters* (Letter 10.96)** | 112 CE | “They worship Christ as a god.” | Provides evidence that early Christians were worshipping Christ as a deity. |

### Why Josephus is considered the earliest

- **Contemporaneity**: Josephus was a first‑century Jewish historian who lived during the reign of Emperor Vespasian (69–79 CE). His *Antiquities* was completed around 93–94 CE, only a few decades after the events he describes.
- **Independent source**: Unlike the New Testament, Josephus was not a Christian writer; his account is part of a broader historical narrative about the Jews and the Roman Empire.
- **Textual integrity**: Modern scholarship generally accepts the core of the “Testimonium Flavianum” (the passage about Jesus) as authentic, though it contains a later Christian interpolation that adds praise for Jesus. Even the “shortened” version, which removes the interpolation, still confirms Jesus’ existence and crucifixion.

### Context of the Josephus passage

> *“Now there was about this time Jesus, a wise man, if it be lawful to call him a man; for he was a doer of wonderful works, a teacher of those who receive the truth, a man who had a following among the Jews and the Gentiles. He was crucified by Pilate, but the Christians who had followed him did not give up their faith.”*  
> — *Antiquities* 18.3.3 (shortened version)

This passage is the earliest surviving reference that mentions Jesus by name, identifies him as a teacher, and records his crucifixion under Pontius Pilate. It is therefore the earliest **historical record** (outside the Christian scriptures) that attests to Jesus Christ’s existence.
